prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” broker that fits everyone — the right choice depends on your exact situation (income, whether you need ACA marketplace coverage or a private/short‑term plan, whether you have employees, whether you want in‑person help, etc.). That said, here’s a practical way to find the best broker for a self‑employed person in the Kansas City area, plus a few options to start with.

How to pick a good broker for a self‑employed person
- Look for experience with individual/ACA plans and with self‑employed finances (1099 sole proprietors).  
- Independent vs. captive: independent brokers can compare many carriers; captive agents only sell one company’s plans. Independents are usually better for comparison shopping.  
- Ask how they are paid (commission vs. flat fee) and whether that affects recommendations.  
- Confirm they’re licensed in Missouri (or Kansas if you live on the KS side) via the state insurance department.  
- Check reviews (Google, Yelp, BBB) and ask for client references, ideally other freelancers/sole proprietors.  
- Make sure they’ll help with subsidy eligibility, enrollment, and year‑round questions (re-enrollment, life changes).

Places/agencies to contact (good starting points)
- Large regional/national brokerages with Kansas City presence: HUB International, Brown & Brown, Gallagher (Arthur J. Gallagher), and NFP. These firms serve small businesses and individual markets and can often help self‑employed clients.  
- National online brokers/comparison sites: eHealthInsurance and Policygenius — good for fast comparisons across carriers (they’re not a local in‑person office, but they handle many individual plans).  
- Local independent brokers and ACA navigators: use Healthcare.gov’s “Find Local Help” or the Missouri Department of Insurance “Agent/Broker Lookup” to find independent brokers or certified enrollment assisters near your ZIP code.

Questions you should ask any broker you interview
- Do you specialize in individual/ACA plans or in small‑group employer plans?  
- How many self‑employed/1099 clients have you helped?  
- Which carriers do you represent and can you show side‑by‑side quotes?  
- How are you compensated? Any fees I should expect?  
- Will you help with subsidy eligibility and Marketplace enrollments?  
- Do you provide year‑round support for life changes and renewals?

If you want, I can:
- Search for and shortlist 3–5 Kansas City brokers who specialize in self‑employed/individual plans (with contact info and ratings), or  
- Walk you through questions to ask and help compare 2–3 specific plan quotes if you share ZIP code, age, household income, and plan preferences.

Which would you like me to do?
